feat(packaging): publish to PyPI and Homebrew, from one set of bytes

simt-dev is a repository tool, and the people running `simt init` inside a
repository are not all Node developers. Somebody adopting a repository with
no package.json has no reason to install a package manager, and a Homebrew
user has no reason to install Node to install a tool that needs Node.

So three channels, one version number, read from package.json rather than
written twice - a second literal drifts, and the drift is invisible until
somebody runs `pip show` beside `simt --version` and gets two answers about
which release they are on.

THE WHEEL IS NOT A WRAPPER. It carries the tool's own source: `files` in
package.json and `force-include` in pyproject.toml name the same paths, and
scripts/verify-wheel.mjs builds both artefacts and hashes every file in both,
failing the release when a single byte differs. A wrapper that ran
`npm install -g simt-dev` on first use is what the unofficial pyright package
does, and it has the properties it is reputed to have: a download on first
run, unpinned, uncacheable, and a failure mode that reads as a broken package
rather than as a missing runtime.

No required dependencies on any channel. The `[node]` extra imports
nodejs_wheel inside a try, at the point of use, never at module level - so
the default install cannot fail on a package it never asked for. ADR-012's
reasoning transfers without modification.

Node is found in an order, not guessed: SIMT_DEV_NODE, the bundled node, then
`node` on PATH - and if none resolve, the remedy rather than a placeholder.
A hardcoded list of /opt/homebrew/bin/node and three friends is three guesses
and a surprise: it prefers a guess over the reader's own PATH.

Homebrew installs the npm tarball and declares depends_on "node". It does NOT
use std_npm_args: that invokes npm at build time, which needs the registry at
build time, to install the one thing here that provably needs neither. The
shebang is rewritten to that node rather than left at env node, so the command
works from a cron job and from a shell that has moved node out of the way -
both of which look identical to a broken install.

The ORDER IS FORCED, NOT CHOSEN. Homebrew downloads from the npm registry at
install time, so a formula naming a version still in npm's staging area
installs a 404 on somebody else's machine, from a release this workflow
already called done. Both jobs fail saying exactly that, and are run again
after `npm stage approve`. Not a workflow_dispatch: on a dispatch
github.ref_name is the branch, and the version guard would compare a tag
against a branch.

Formula/simt-dev.rb is the source of truth and release-formula.mjs patches
two lines in it, anchored on content rather than line number - a line number
makes the formula a file that cannot be edited, because adding a comment
above the sha256 line would silently write the checksum to the wrong place.
A template would mean the bytes a reader sees here are not the bytes a tap
serves, which is the defect ADR-023 ruled out for the gate file.

Verified, not assumed:

  - the wheel was installed into a venv and `simt --version`,
    `simt rules why ADR-018` and `simt graph lint` all ran from it
  - the formula was audited (brew audit --strict, clean), installed from a
    throwaway tap, and ran the same three commands from the Cellar
  - verify-wheel.mjs reports 128 paths byte-identical across npm and PyPI,
    and was tampered with to prove it fails - a wheel-only README.md made it
    fail with that stated
  - all four node-resolution paths exercised: env override, good and bad;
    PATH; and no node at all, which prints the remedy and exits 2

The parity check is a release script and NOT a test, deliberately. The tests
hold the static invariants - same paths, one version, one command, stdlib
only - and run in npm test with no network and no interpreter. The one that
cannot be static runs in the workflow where a Python and a registry exist by
construction. A test that needed pip would not run for the next person who
clones this, and would run differently on the machine that wrote it.

Two findings from the first run are recorded in the ADR because they are the
kind that only appear when a check is real: it flagged LICENSE and README.md
as differences (both are tarball metadata, not wheel files), and it flagged
bin, src, graph and rules as missing from both, because `files` names
DIRECTORIES and npm expands them recursively.

test/rules.test.mjs gained ADR-058 on the prose-location count. The record is
about three specific files, and an argument about which file a rule lives in
that declines to name any file is not an argument.

ADR-058. 748 pass, 0 fail from an isolated sibling-free copy. `simt ci --yes`
added the pip ecosystem to dependabot by itself - the detection ruling in
ADR-013 working, with no code change.
